properties.chose: Option (c1): move onto flo2.io and commit a copy per PR, as flo2 does. (a), keep it local, would leave the one local member unwatched once flo2.io reads a hub's members in-host. (b), wait for position 11, keeps the copy problem for longer. (c2), no design in the repo, stays the end state at position 11.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27: "I was going to say we could put the reflow2 there also, but I'm concerned that we don't have all the tools. then again, if I keep this dev_reflow2 at running locally, it would still have all 193 tools."

TODAY: reflow2's design is a local store beside its repository, reached by the hub's child-reflow2 connection with all 193 tools. The combined plan moves it last among the moves (position 11, after flo2's), as dec:idea-a-repo-that-holds-its-design-moves-it-to-a-remote-server-once set.

WHAT THE CONCERN TURNS ON, measured the same night:
- The tools actually missing through api.flo2.io are fewer than 17. Of the 17 flo2 refuses, seven take their evidence from the caller and read nothing on the host (flo2's fact:only-wall-check-of-the-machine-side-tools-reads-files-itself-2026-09-27); flo2 schedules five of them at combined position 2, and the other two are the same kind. What genuinely stays missing is wall_check (it reads the files itself), the seven that read other designs by path (combined position 12), and two that stay off by design.
- ⚠️ "KEEP dev_reflow2 LOCAL WITH ALL 193" ONLY HOLDS FOR DESIGNS WHOSE STORE IS ON THIS MACHINE. The hub reaches each child through that child's own server. A design moved to flo2.io is reached through flo2.io's gateway, and reflow2's local client (`--remote`) forwards to that same gateway, so it gets the same 176 today. A local server cannot serve the full list for a design it does not hold.
- reflow2's own work leans harder on the missing and not-yet-remote pieces than flo2's does: CI runs wall_check against the design, release cuts freeze checksums measured on the build machine (position 10), and the export-based CI gate (position 9).
- 🛑 BOOTSTRAP, SHARPER THAN FOR flo2: flo2.io's engine IS reflow2. An engine release that breaks opening designs would also make reflow2's design, the one you would read to fix it, unreachable from flo2.io.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) Keep reflow2's design local for good; flo2.io hosts everyone else's. Cheapest; gives up "one blueprint on a server" for the engine's own design.
(b) Move it where the plan has it (11), once CI, release cuts and wall_check have a remote route.
(c) Move it early and accept the gaps. The largest cost of the three: reflow2's CI and release process depend on exactly what is missing.

═══ 2026-09-30 — @AJS BRAINSTORMS THE MOVE AGAIN. RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING; nothing chosen. ═══
In his words: "I really want to figure out how to push reflow2 to flo2.io, but I believe there is some issues with how changelog.md is updated and how the design is tracked in the reflow2 github repo. If the design is held in flo2.io for reflow2, could just before a PR, could we export the design, download it locally and then update the change log accordingly and then merge? The design is then always up to speed with that last PR. We could also remove the design completely from the reflow2 design and then only have to worry about how to figure out how to update the change log?"

HIS TWO SHAPES, mapped onto what is already settled:
(c1) MOVE NOW AND COMMIT A COPY PER PR, which is option (c) with flo2's bridge. Before merge, take the copy from flo2.io and commit it as the PR's last commit; CI reads it. This is exactly how flo2 works today (flo2 cap:flo2s-design-is-hosted-and-ci-reads-a-copy; used today by flo2 #110).
(c2) MOVE AND KEEP NO DESIGN IN THE REPO. This is the settled END STATE: combined position 11 retires the copy, under dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy. It is planned AFTER position 9 (epoch:planned-ci-asks-the-blueprint), because without it CI has no design to check the code against.

THE PAIN HE NAMES IS REAL, and measured in this repo:
- every parallel PR carries an export, so the design file conflicts, needs the merge driver, and once showed a ~115-line change as a ~380,000-line rewrite (fact:the-merge-driver-writes-the-merged-export-in-a-different-byte-layout-than-the-exporter-2026-09-22);
- #620's CI failed when its export grew;
- branch records need worktree-private stores, and live records need folding back (#637);
- the live store sits on whatever branch the checkout is on: 2026-09-30, 19 commits behind main, and a status read from it was wrong;
- CHANGELOG's Unreleased section conflicts on every parallel PR. That half is recorded separately on dec:idea-how-changelog-md-gets-written-once-the-design-is-the-record.

FOR (c1):
- It removes the three-way design merge. The server is the one truth, so at merge time the PR simply re-copies the latest; there is nothing to reconcile.
- It keeps reflow2's design PUBLIC: the repo copy is public, and flo2.io designs are private, with "make a design public" planned, not built.
- The newest copy in git is the bootstrap fallback this node's 🛑 asks for: a broken engine release can be recovered from it by local import.

AGAINST (c1), kept beside it:
- The blocker was never the copy. reflow2's own loop leans on what api.flo2.io does not yet serve: wall_check, local-file measurement against a remote design (position 7), the eight path-reading tools (position 12), and release-cut checksums on the build machine (position 10).
- With one hosted design, a branch's design writes land in the SHARED design before merge. Parallel branches see each other's in-flight records, and an abandoned PR leaves records for code that never merged. Today's worktree-private stores exist to prevent exactly that. It is open question (c) of the photocopy decision, unanswered.
- flo2's copy script has a measured gap: ops/flo2-design-copy cannot pass accept_divergence, so a deliberate edge removal blocked it on 2026-09-30.

SIZE: (c1) is medium. Copy plus CI already exist for flo2. The cost is the per-branch-records question and working without the unserved tools.
(c2) is large and ordered. It needs position 9: CI reaching flo2.io means a credential in a PUBLIC repo's CI, and fork PRs cannot read secrets. #616 came from an outside team. It also loses public readability until public designs exist.

═══ 2026-09-30, LATER — @AJS ASKS FOR "IDEAS TO COUNTERACT" THE TWO OBJECTIONS TO (c1). Recorded as brainstorming; nothing chosen. ═══

OBJECTION 2 (branch records in one hosted design) already has a designed answer, waiting for his word: dec:how-a-branchs-implementation-facts-are-held. Its option (a) is a per-branch overlay; option (d), added today, is design changes replayed from the PR at merge. The hosted-specific consequences are noted there.

OBJECTION 1 (the tools api.flo2.io does not serve) is mostly answered by accepted intent and planned steps:
- req:the-local-client-opens-the-persons-files-for-the-tools-that-name-one (accepted): wall_check and the seven path-reading tools run through the person's own client, which opens the files locally;
- combined position 7: local files are measured for a remote design;
- combined position 10: a release cut against a remote design;
- combined position 12: the file-opening tools.
Today's options here are about ORDER and INTERIM, not about whether:
(i) PULL 7, 10 AND 12 FORWARD as the move's critical path, ahead of positions they do not depend on.
(ii) MOVE THE FRONT DOOR, NOT THE STORE. flo2.io routes callers to a reflow2 design whose home stays on the machine that holds the repository, where every tool works (flo2's req:any-node-serves-a-caller-to-the-design-wherever-it-lives, proposed; its capability planned). People reach reflow2's design through flo2.io, while its store and files stay together.
  - AGAINST: the design is reachable only while that machine is up, and exposing a home machine to flo2's gateway is a new attack surface. It also does not retire the local server.
(iii) CI AS THE FILE-MEASURING CLIENT. CI holds the checkout. It runs the local client against the hosted design and sends checksums as asserted, which covers positions 7 and 9 for the gate.
  - AGAINST: CI then needs a flo2.io credential, which a public repo's fork PRs cannot read.

SIZES: (i) is the plan's own work, re-ordered. (ii) is medium-large on flo2's side, plus an operational risk. (iii) is medium, and inherits the credential problem.



═══ SETTLED 2026-10-09 — OPTION (c1): MOVE, AND COMMIT A COPY PER PR ═══
Anthony, 2026-10-09, dev_reflow2 hub, asked how this hub should eventually watch its members (a design on flo2.io cannot watch another), chose "Move reflow2's design onto flo2.io too" over waiting for in-host reads with reflow2 left local, and over moving the hub back to local.

WHY NOW: flo2 accepted the same day that a flo2.io hub's designs are read there, as the caller (flo2's req:a-flo2-io-hubs-designs-are-its-members-for-reflow2s-hub-work-read-in-host-as-the-caller). Those reads reach only designs flo2.io holds. reflow2's design is the one member of the dev_reflow2 family that is local, so it would stay unwatched. Moving it puts the whole family on one host.

THE SHAPE: (c1). The design lives on flo2.io. Before a PR merges, a copy is taken from flo2.io and committed, and CI reads that copy, as flo2 does (flo2 cap:flo2s-design-is-hosted-and-ci-reads-a-copy). The copy is written in the item layout by the PR's own reflow2, so its stamp and its chain are this repo's. The copy retires later at combined position 11, as already planned.

WHAT STANDS, AND MUST BE PLANNED BEFORE THE MOVE, not discovered after:
- 🛑 THE BOOTSTRAP RISK: flo2.io's engine IS reflow2. An engine release that breaks opening designs must not leave reflow2's design unreachable, so the committed copy, plus a store backup, must be enough to work from locally.
- A release cut writes its record with the NEW binary while flo2.io runs the previous one. The copy is imported and re-exported by the cut's own binary, as flo2's design-copy does.
- wall_check, and the tools that open another design by path, are not served on flo2.io. Wherever reflow2's CI or cut uses them, they run against the committed copy locally.
- The PR-based recording used until now (a scratch store, export, commit) is replaced by writing to the hosted design, then the copy.



═══ THE PLAN, AND PHASE 0, 2026-10-09 ═══
MEASURED FOR THE PLAN:
- flo2.io accepts the id `reflow2` (the gateway's pattern is ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$), so no pin or cross-design reference anywhere in the family has to change. flo2's own ops/flo2-design-copy refuses a non-hex id, and reflow2 needs its own copy script anyway, for the item layout.
- The design is 6,955 nodes and 46,799 edges: a 26 MB store and a 30 MB single-file export. All 24 hosted designs together take 230 MB.
- The droplet has 2,980 of 3,915 MB free; its engine holds 209 MB.
- reflow2's CI runs no tool flo2.io refuses. It only tests wall_check itself, locally.

THE PROBLEM THE PLAN HAD TO ANSWER: with one live design, PR B's design writes are in the design before B merges. PR A's copy would then carry B's accepted checksums against files A's branch does not have, and A's design gate fails on B's work.
Anthony, 2026-10-09, chose "One design PR at a time": one design-writing PR in flight at a time, the copy taken last after merging main, and a copy script that refuses while another PR's changes are in the live design. He chose it over replaying local records after merge, which keeps parallel work but leaves the hosted design lagging during development, defeating the move. The cost accepted: no stacked design work such as items 4-6 of 2026-10-08.
ALSO NOTED: design records land live before their PR is reviewed. The committed copy still shows them in the PR's diff, but undoing one is a new write, not a closed PR.

PHASE 0 (Anthony: "Phase 0 rehearsal, then report"): a throwaway 0.81.0 server on the droplet, its own temporary folder and port, removed afterwards.
- Import 6.8 s; open 3.3 s; search, get_node, scan_nodes and open_questions under 0.1 s; relation_candidates 0.5 s; export 4.5-4.9 s.
- loop_status took 46.3 s cold and 30.8 s warm, against the gateway's 30 s limit per engine call (httpReflow2's default; server.ts sets none). That was the blocker.
- Root cause: the confirmation ledger re-read each artifact's history once per capability (fact:the-confirmation-ledger-re-read-every-artifacts-history-once-per-capability-2026-10-09). Fixed in #707.
- With the fix, on the droplet: 11.7 s cold and 0.8 s warm; peak 677 MB for this design. Not yet released, so flo2.io would run the slow ledger until the next release.

NEXT: phase 1 (the copy script with the one-PR guard, AGENTS.md's recording path, the release-cut changes, a break-glass note) waits on Anthony's go. A release must carry #707 before phase 2, the move.



═══ PHASE 1, BUILT 2026-10-10 (Anthony: "Merge 708, 710 and begin phase 1") ═══
WHAT IT IS: tools/reflow2_design_copy.py, with three verbs: hold, copy and status (cap:a-design-pr-holds-reflow2s-hosted-design-and-copies-it-in-last). The copy reads the hosted design from flo2.io's engine over ssh (a read). It drops the hold claims, imports the rest into a throwaway store with this repo's binary, and exports the item layout into docs/design/reflow2/.

THE GUARD, AND ONE CHOICE MADE WITHOUT ANTHONY, FLAGGED FOR HIS WORD: the hold is a claim on the existing claim board (claim_region on proj:reflow2, depth 0, note "design PR: <branch>").
- Why: it is attributed and visible to every session on the design (claim_report), and it needs no new schema and nothing on flo2.io's box. Claims are advisory, so the refusal lives in the script that every design PR must pass to reach main.
- "In flight" is computed: what the live design holds that main's copy does not, hold claims aside. So there is no release step: after a merge nothing is in flight, and the hold is stale.
- Considered and not taken:
  - a GitHub label on the PR: the PR would have to exist before the first write, so an empty commit, and an outside contributor cannot label;
  - a hold file on the droplet: reachable only by ssh, and invisible to agents working on the design;
  - a property on proj:reflow2: every PR's copy would then change the project node.
- What it cannot do: a session that writes without holding is not caught. Writes nobody holds are named by hold and copy, and need --adopt.

MEASURED 2026-10-10 on the real design (6,976 nodes, 47,571 edges):
- The import-export round trip is exact on 0.81.1.
- An export written by 0.81.0 keeps its content hash through 0.81.1, which is the cut's case.
- A copy with nothing changed writes no item.
- A rehearsal with one added requirement and a hold wrote exactly that one item file, and refused another branch with the holder named. It took 42 s.
- The read path, run against the hub's hosted design (reflow2's is not hosted yet), returned it in 2.3 s with its content hash intact.
- The default host is the droplet's IP, as in every flo2 ops script, since this machine's known_hosts names the IP.

THE RELEASE CUT: once the design is moved, the cut records on flo2.io (still on the previous release), and step 6 is the copy taken by the cut's own binary. This is written into AGENTS.md and onto step 6 (cap:a-cut-exports-the-record-once-from-the-new-binary).

BREAK GLASS (AGENTS.md):
- Work locally from the committed copy.
- Writes made on flo2.io and not yet copied come back from flo2.io's nightly store backup, through copy --from.
- Local writes go back by writing them again on flo2.io, or by an operator replacing the hosted store, with Anthony's go.
No new backup is needed: flo2's nightly backup already archives every hosted design's store.

NEXT: phase 2, the move, which needs Anthony's go because it writes on flo2.io's box. It puts the design on flo2.io under the id `reflow2` from main's committed copy, points this repo's MCP configuration at it, takes the first hold-and-copy on a real PR, and flips AGENTS.md's "until the move lands".
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-09 — reflow2's own design moves onto flo2.io (option c1: hosted, with a copy committed per PR for CI), so in-host reads cover the whole family
